farraa:1-2.t: [126/a] His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿عَبَسَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ أَن جَآءَهُ ٱلأَعْمَىٰ﴾. That was ʿAbd Allāh ibn Umm Maktūm — Umm Maktūm was his father's mother. He came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while there was with him a group of the nobles of Quraysh, to ask about something from which he would benefit; and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked that he should interrupt his talk. So Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, sent down: ﴿عَبَسَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ﴾, meaning Muhammad ﷺ, ﴿أَن جَآءَهُ ٱلأَعْمَىٰ﴾: because the blind man came to him.

farraa:3-4.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿وَمَا يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّهُ يَزَّكَّىٰ﴾.
By what he wanted to learn of your knowledge. Then the Prophet ﷺ turned with kindness to Ibn Umm Maktūm [«على أن ابن أم مكتوم» in the source — Translator's note: «أن» appears to be an intrusion], and honoured him after this verse, to the point that he appointed him as his deputy to lead the prayer. The readers agreed on: ﴿فَتَنفَعَهُ ٱلذِّكْرَىٰ﴾ with the nominative [Translator's note: so in the source, although the vowelled quotation shows the accusative فتنفعَه; the readings are reported the other way round elsewhere]; if it were accusative as the response of the fāʾ to لعلّ, it would be correct.
Someone recited to me:
علَّ صروفَ الدَّهر أو دولاتِها * يُدلْنَنَا اللَّمَّة من لَمّاتها
فتستريحَ النفس من زفْراتها * وتُنْقعَ الغلَّةُ من غُلاتها
(Perhaps the vicissitudes of time or its turns will grant us a turn from among its turns, so that the soul may rest from its sighs and the burning thirst be quenched.)
Some read: "أأن جاءه الأعمى" with two hamzas with fatḥa, i.e.: because the blind man came to him he frowned; and it is like His saying: "أأنْ كان ذا مالٍ وبَنِينَ".

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَنتَ لَهُ تَصَدَّىٰ﴾.
If a reader read: "تَصَدّى" [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably the passive تُصَدَّى is meant], it would be correct.

farraa:11-13.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَلاَّ إِنَّهَا تَذْكِرَةٌ﴾.
This sura is a reminder. If you wish, you make the hāʾ a support (ʿimād) because of the feminine of التذكرة.
﴿فَمَن شَآءَ ذَكَرَهُ﴾:
he remembers the Qurʾān; the masculine [pronoun] goes back to the revelation.
﴿فَي صُحُفٍ مُّكَرَّمَةٍ﴾:
because they came down from the Preserved Tablet, raised high with your Lord there, purified; none touches them but the purified. This is like His saying: ﴿فَالْمُدَبِّرَاتِ أَمْراً﴾.
He made [126/b] the angels and the scrolls purified, because purification applies to the scrolls, so He made purification belong to those who carry them as well.

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بِأَيْدِي سَفَرَةٍ﴾.
They are the angels; the singular is سافر. The Arabs say: سفرت بين القوم (I mediated between the people) when you make peace between them. So the angels, when they descend with the revelation of Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, and His instruction, were made like the envoy (السفير) who makes peace between people. The poet said:
وما أدعُ السِّفارةَ بينَ قومى * وما أمْشى بغشٍّ إن مَشَيْتُ
(I do not abandon mediation among my people, and I do not go about with deceit when I go.)
And البررة: its singular, by analogy in Arabic, is بارّ; because the Arabs do not say فَعَلة intending a plural unless its singular is فاعل, like كافر and كفرة, and فاجر and فجرة. This is the rule, by which its singular is بارّ. What the Arabs [actually] say is: رجل بَرّ (a pious man) and امرأة برّة (a pious woman); then it was given a plural on the interpretation of فاعل, as they said: قوم خَيَرَة بَرَرَة (good, pious people) — I heard it from one of the Arabs — and the singular of الخيرة is خيّر, and of البررة: برّ. Similar to it is: قوم سَراة (noble people), whose singular is سَرِيّ; it ought to have been سارٍ. When the Arabs pluralise سارٍ they pluralise it with a ḍamma on the first letter and say: سُراة and غُزاة. So it is as though, when they said سَراة, they disliked giving its first letter a ḍamma, which would make the singular seem to be سارٍ; so they wanted to distinguish, by the fatḥa on the first letter of سَراة, between السريّ and الساري.

farraa:17-19.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَآ أَكْفَرَهُ﴾.
It may be an exclamation of wonder, and it may be: what is it that made him disbelieve? The exegesis came with this second interpretation. Then He made him wonder and said: ﴿مِنْ أَيِّ شَيءٍ خَلَقَهُ﴾. Then [127/a] He explained and said: ﴿مِن نُّطْفَةٍ خَلَقَهُ فَقَدَّرَهُ﴾ — in stages: a drop, then a clot, to the end of his creation; and wretched or happy, and male or female.

farraa:20-20.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ ٱلسَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُ﴾.
Its meaning: then He made him at ease with the way (يسّره للسبيل). Similar to it is: ﴿إِنَّا هَدَيْنَاهُ السَّبِيلَ﴾, i.e. We made known to him the way of good and the way of evil.

farraa:21-21.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ أَمَاتَهُ فَأَقْبَرَهُ﴾.
He made him one who is buried, and did not make him one of those thrown to the beasts of prey and the birds, nor one of those placed in ossuaries (النواويس); as though the grave is one of the things by which the Muslim was honoured. He did not say فقبره, because القابر is the one who buries with his hand, while المُقبِر is Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, because He made him one who has a grave; and His act is not like the act of the human (الآمى) [Translator's note: so in the source; read الآدمي]. The Arabs say: بترتُ ذنب البعير (I cut off the camel's tail), and والله أبتره (and Allah made it tailless).
And عضبت قرن الثور (I broke the bull's horn), and والله أعضبه (Allah made it broken-horned); and طردت فلاناً عني (I drove So-and-so away from me), and والله أطرده, i.e. He made him an outcast. If someone said فقبره, or said of a human أقبره when he directs it in his sense, it would be acceptable and correct. Do you not see that you say: "So-and-so killed his brother", and another says: "Allah killed him"? The Arabs say: هذه كلمة مُقتِلة مُخيفة (this is a word that gets one killed, that brings fear) when whoever says it would be killed; it is said thus, and if one said of it قاتلة خائفة, it would be correct, as you say: هذا الداء قاتلك (this disease is killing you).

farraa:23-23.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿كَلاَّ لَمَّا يَقْضِ مَآ أَمَرَهُ﴾.
He has not fulfilled some of what He commanded him.

farraa:25-25.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَنَّا صَبَبْنَا ٱلْمَآءَ صَبّاً﴾.
Al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim read (أنّا), making it in the position of the genitive, i.e.: let him look at Our pouring the water, [i.e.] to [the fact] that We poured, and did such and such. The people of the Ḥijāz and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī read (إنّا), giving information about the description of the food by way of resumption (istiʾnāf); and both are good. Likewise His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَانْظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقبةُ مَكْرِهِمْ أَنَّا دَمَّرْنَاهُمْ﴾ and ﴿إِنا دمرناهم﴾. The position of "أنّا" here in (ʿAbasa), when it has a fatḥa, may also be nominative, as though He resumed and said: his food is Our pouring the water and Our causing such and such to grow.

farraa:27-27.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿حَبّاً﴾.
الحب: all grains — wheat, barley and what is besides them. القضب: fresh fodder (الرطبة); the people of Mecca call fodder (القتّ) القضب. الحدائق: every garden that has a wall around it is a حديقة; what has no wall around it is not called حديقة. الغُلْب: what is thick among the palm trees. الأبّ: what the livestock eat. That is what Ibn ʿAbbās said.

farraa:32-32.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿مَّتَاعاً لَّكُمْ﴾.
That is: We created it as an enjoyment for you and a benefit. If it were nominative, it would be permissible, as we have explained.

farraa:33-33.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلصَّآخَّةُ﴾: the Resurrection.

farraa:34-34.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَوْمَ يَفِرُّ ٱلْمَرْءُ مِنْ أَخِيهِ﴾.
He flees from his brother: من and عن are the same in it.

farraa:37-37.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِكُلِّ ٱمْرِىءٍ مِّنْهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ شَأْنٌ يُغْنِيهِ﴾.
That is: it occupies him away from his kin. One of the readers read: "يعنيه" (concerns him), and that is anomalous (shādhdh).

farraa:38-38.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ مُّسْفِرَةٌ﴾.
Shining, bright. When a woman casts off her veil or her face-cover, it is said: سفرت, so she is سافر; and one does not say أسفرت.

farraa:41-41.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تَرْهَقُهَا قَتَرَةٌ﴾.
In speech, قَتْرة, with the tāʾ vowelless, is permissible; but no one has read it so.
